title: rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration floor-divides to zero when budget < windowDuration, stranding dust and enabling the F-04 zero-rate modifier bypass
regression-risk: pre-existing (prior CS-02, rejected as Medium but dust-stranding remains)
description:
Every rate-computation site uses floor division: `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration`. When `rewardBudget < windowDuration` (in seconds), the result truncates to zero and `_updatePool` accrues no rewards. More subtly, each reset also truncates the sub-windowDuration residue, so the unconditional resets in `_syncBudget` compound a small amount of dust into stranded funds over pool lifetime.

With `MAX_WINDOW = 10 * 365 days = 315,360,000 seconds`, residue below ~3.15e8 wei per reset stays stranded. Per-reset loss is tiny (~3.15e-10 phUSD), but resets happen on every `_syncBudget` call (which is every meaningful user interaction), so the total grows with pool activity.

This also creates the zero-rate vacuous-pass case in the `ownerOrNotGriefed` modifier (see F-04 instance C): when `rewardRate == 0`, the modifier's `rewardRate >= rPre` clause is trivially true, allowing indefinite window extensions against a zero-rate schedule.
impact: Small, bounded per-reset dust stranding. Accumulates over pool lifetime but remains sub-nanocent per reset. The more serious secondary impact is that it enables the F-04 modifier bypass under zero-rate conditions — a griefer can drive the rate to zero (by working with small residue states) and then indefinitely extend the window.
proof:
Case 1 (truncation of residue): `rewardBudget = 1e8 wei`, `windowDuration = 540 days`. `rewardRate = 1e8/46656000 = 2 wei/sec`. Over 540 days total emission = 93,312,000 wei — NOT 1e8. 6,688,000 wei stranded.

Case 2 (zero rate): `rewardBudget = 1e7 wei` (below windowDuration in seconds). `rewardRate = 0`. No emissions. All 1e7 wei stranded until a top-up raises budget above 46,656,000 wei. While in this state, any non-owner call to `pullAndRefresh` / `topUp` passes the modifier (zero >= zero) and can reset `windowEnd` indefinitely.
suggested-fix: Use higher-precision rate: `rewardRate = (rewardBudget * ACC_PRECISION) / windowDuration`, and in `_updatePool` compute `reward = (elapsed * rewardRate) / ACC_PRECISION`. This shifts truncation down by 18 decimals, effectively eliminating stranding and the zero-rate edge case. Alternatively, track accrual directly as `rewardBudget * elapsed / windowDuration` and drop the stored `rewardRate` variable.
consolidation-note: No direct ES overlap. Closely linked to F-04 instance C; preserved separately because the root cause (floor division) is distinct from the modifier-logic root cause and the fix (precision scaling) is orthogonal. Fixing F-08 eliminates the F-04 zero-rate case but not the expired-window or truncation-boundary cases.
